issues.description: Guard predicate is too broad — fires for every non-Tab key, not just Enter/Return.
issues.detail: The condition `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` captures Escape, arrows, Backspace, and modifiers, not just the Enter/Return case the author intended. The contract should explicitly restrict the branch to `key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter)` so navigation and dismissal keys retain their existing behavior.

issues.description: Manually re-dispatching the event into textedit.keyPressEvent leaks abstraction and bypasses Qt propagation.
issues.detail: Calling `self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` from the popup couples the completion widget to the editor's internal input pipeline and risks double-handling if Qt also propagates. The correct discipline is to hide the popup and call `event.ignore()` (or accept), letting Qt's normal event propagation deliver the key to the editor.

issues.description: Condition is written awkwardly — `not X and not key == Y` instead of a named guard.
issues.detail: Bind the conf lookup to a named local and use `!=` rather than `not ==`: `if not enter_accepts and key != Qt.Key_Tab`. The current phrasing relies on Python operator precedence rather than stating intent, and reads as transcription rather than reasoning about the predicate.

issues.description: get_conf is called on every keystroke inside the popup's hot path.
issues.detail: Reading the configuration system on each keyPressEvent couples a hot input path to the conf subsystem unnecessarily. Cache the value when the popup is shown or subscribe to option changes, then read the cached local in the handler.

issues.description: New branch is spliced ahead of the existing `item is None` precondition without restating the contract.
issues.detail: The surrounding acceptance logic assumes a current item exists before deciding to accept/dismiss; the new hide+forward path runs before that guard regardless of selection state. Move the early-exit guard above the currentItem() lookup and document which keys accept, dismiss, or navigate so subclasses can preserve substitutability.

issues.description: PR ships a behavioral switch with no tests and no stated specification for either branch.
issues.detail: No automated test exercises either branch of the new option, and neither the config default nor the conf-page tip states the full contract (Enter/Return pass through when False; Tab still accepts; arrows navigate; Escape dismisses). Add a test exhibiting both branches and a docstring stating the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR adds a useful preference but the implementation is unsound. The guard predicate is too broad — it fires for every non-Tab key rather than just Enter/Return — and the handler re-dispatches the event directly into textedit.keyPressEvent, leaking the editor's event pipeline into the completion widget and risking double-handling. The expression is also awkwardly phrased (`not X and not key == Y`) and reads the config on every keystroke. Required fixes: narrow the predicate to Return/Enter, replace manual re-dispatch with hide() + event.ignore(), cache the conf lookup, and add a test plus a written contract for the new option.
